text: A create flow in which the server generates the token, stores only its SHA-256 hash, and returns the plaintext once in the create response.
The 10-active-token limit is enforced at create time and refuses the request with a 'revoke one first' message.
A list flow that returns name, created date, expiry date and last-used time ('Never' if unused) for active tokens only, and never returns the secret.
Token authentication on an API call through the Bearer header, returning the same generic 401 for missing, unknown, revoked or expired tokens.
A last-used update that is triggered by successful authentication and limited to about one write per token per hour, not one write per request.
A revoke flow, limited to the user's own tokens, that makes the very next request with that token fail with 401.
A 90-day expiry that is recorded at creation and checked on every API call.
Delivered as a Mermaid sequenceDiagram with short notes before or after it, including the lost-create-response case.
